# Overview

The recode notebook reports the ladder as **composition**: GC, GC3, third-base
percentages, percentiles against the expressed background. Those numbers are
what the design was matched on, but they are not what gets ordered, and they
cannot answer "which codon sits at position 412, and did we change it?" The
assembled sequences exist only as a single flat string per construct in
`08_recoded_assembled_sequences_*.csv`. This notebook is the codon-level
reading of those same strings.

Two things are shown, and a third is checked on the way:

1. **Where every codon is, and which ones were touched.** A tile map of all
   four rungs at codon resolution, colored by third base, plus the same grid
   colored by whether the codon was recoded, left alone, or structurally
   unable to change. Then the sequences printed out codon by codon with the
   same coloring, as a lab reference to read against a synthesis order.
2. **Whether the chosen codons track MDA-MB-231 usage.** The recoder samples
   each position's codon in proportion to the pooled synonymous usage of the
   expressed transcriptome, but only *after* the third base has been forced by
   the GC3 target. Those two steps pull in different directions, so this is
   measured in two panels: raw, which shows the composition constraint's
   footprint, and within each (amino acid, third base) cell, which isolates the
   sampler from the constraint.

**This notebook re-derives the originals rather than reading them.** Showing
*changed vs unchanged* needs the pre-recode sequences and *free vs fixed* needs
the part boundaries, and neither is in the exported files. So the parts are
re-imported from `cds seq.xlsx` and the original ladder is rebuilt here, the
same way `08_` builds it, then diffed against the exported recoded sequences.
That is a benefit rather than a cost: the diff is an independent check that the
exported sequences really are synonymous with the originals, run outside the
notebook that produced them.

Nothing here is random. The recoding already happened; this reads its output.

# 1. Load Libraries

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(Biostrings)
library(scales)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7)

indir  <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design")
outdir <- indir
```

# 2. Import and Verify the Parts

Identical import and verification to `07_` and `08_`, so all three notebooks
are provably building from the same parts.

```{r read_parts}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

parts_tbl <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(parts_tbl)[1] <- "construct"

parts <- parts_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
stopifnot("Duplicate part names in cds seq.xlsx" = !any(duplicated(parts$part)))
pseq <- setNames(parts$seq, parts$part)

needed <- c("smbit n", "p2a", "flag3x", "egfp", "waldo linker")
stopifnot(
  "A required part is missing from cds seq.xlsx" = all(needed %in% names(pseq)),
  "A part contains non-ACGT characters" = all(!grepl("[^ACGT]", pseq[needed])),
  "A part is not divisible by 3" = all(nchar(pseq[needed]) %% 3 == 0)
)

smbit_n <- pseq[["smbit n"]]
p2a     <- pseq[["p2a"]]
flag3x  <- pseq[["flag3x"]]
egfp    <- pseq[["egfp"]]
waldo   <- pseq[["waldo linker"]]
flag1x  <- substr(flag3x, 43, 66)

aa_of <- function(s) as.character(translate(DNAString(s)))

stopifnot(
  "smBit n does not encode Met + the SmBiT peptide" =
    aa_of(smbit_n) == "MVTGYRLFEEIL",
  "p2a does not encode the expected 19-aa P2A peptide" =
    aa_of(p2a) == "ATNFSLLKQAGDVEENPGP",
  "1xFLAG does not encode the DYKDDDDK epitope" = aa_of(flag1x) == "DYKDDDDK",
  "egfp is not 723 nt" = nchar(egfp) == 723,
  "egfp protein does not carry the TYG chromophore at residues 66-68" =
    substr(aa_of(egfp), 66, 68) == "TYG",
  "waldo linker does not encode GSAGSAAGSGEF" = aa_of(waldo) == "GSAGSAAGSGEF"
)
cat("Parts verified.\n")
```

## The original ladder, rebuilt

```{r rebuild_originals}
gfp_copies <- 0:params$max_gfp_copies
originals  <- {
  bb <- paste0(smbit_n, p2a, flag1x)
  map_chr(gfp_copies, function(n)
    if (n == 0) bb else paste0(bb, strrep(paste0(waldo, egfp), n)))
}
names(originals) <- ifelse(gfp_copies == 0, "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG",
                           sprintf("SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-%dxeGFP", gfp_copies))
cat("Rebuilt", length(originals), "original rungs:",
    paste(nchar(originals), collapse = ", "), "nt\n")
```

## The part layout, in codons

Every construct is the same four-part backbone followed by *k* repeats of
linker + eGFP. Only FLAG and the eGFP copies were free to change: SmBiT, P2A
and the Waldo linker are held fixed by `08_`, the linker because it carries the
in-frame EcoRI site the cloning depends on.

```{r part_layout}
n_cod <- function(s) nchar(s) %/% 3L

# One row per contiguous stretch of codons, in order along the construct.
layout_for <- function(k) {
  base <- tibble(
    part  = c("SmBiT", "P2A", "FLAG"),
    ncod  = c(n_cod(smbit_n), n_cod(p2a), n_cod(flag1x)),
    state = c("fixed", "fixed", "free")
  )
  if (k == 0) return(base)
  reps <- map_dfr(seq_len(k), ~ tibble(
    part  = c("linker", sprintf("eGFP copy %d", .x)),
    ncod  = c(n_cod(waldo), n_cod(egfp)),
    state = c("fixed", "free")
  ))
  bind_rows(base, reps)
}

layout_tbl <- map_dfr(set_names(gfp_copies, names(originals)), layout_for,
                      .id = "construct") %>%
  group_by(construct) %>%
  mutate(end = cumsum(ncod), start = end - ncod + 1L) %>%
  ungroup()

stopifnot(
  "Part layout does not account for every codon in a construct" =
    all((layout_tbl %>% group_by(construct) %>%
           summarise(tot = sum(ncod), .groups = "drop") %>%
           arrange(match(construct, names(originals))))$tot ==
          map_int(originals, n_cod))
)
print(layout_tbl %>% filter(construct == names(originals)[length(originals)]) %>%
        dplyr::select(part, state, start, end) %>% as.data.frame())
```

# 3. Read the Recoded Sequences

```{r read_recoded}
seq_csv <- file.path(indir,
             paste0("08_recoded_assembled_sequences_", params$run_tag, ".csv"))
use_csv <- file.path(indir,
             paste0("08_codon_usage_231_", params$run_tag, ".csv"))
stopifnot(
  "Recoded sequences not found: knit 08_ first" = file.exists(seq_csv),
  "Codon usage table not found: re-knit 08_, which now exports it" =
    file.exists(use_csv)
)

rec_tbl <- read_csv(seq_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
recoded <- setNames(rec_tbl$cds, rec_tbl$construct)

stopifnot(
  "Recoded CSV does not hold the expected rungs" =
    identical(sort(names(recoded)), sort(names(originals))),
  "A recoded sequence contains non-ACGT characters" =
    all(!grepl("[^ACGT]", recoded))
)
recoded <- recoded[names(originals)]          # same order as the originals
cat("Read", length(recoded), "recoded rungs with tag", params$run_tag, "\n")
```

## Independent check that the recoding is synonymous

`08_` asserts this on the objects it just built. Re-asserting it here on the
*exported file*, with the originals rebuilt from the spreadsheet, closes the
gap between what was validated and what will be ordered.

```{r validate_exported}
walk2(recoded, originals, function(new, old) {
  stopifnot(
    "An exported rung differs in length from the original" =
      nchar(new) == nchar(old),
    "An exported rung changed the protein" = aa_of(new) == aa_of(old),
    "An exported rung carries a stop codon" =
      !any(codon_split(new) %in% STOP_CODONS)
  )
})
cat("Every exported rung is synonymous with its original.\n")

# Discriminative companion: the files must actually differ from the originals.
# A pipeline that exported its input would pass every assertion above.
n_changed <- map2_int(recoded, originals,
                      ~ sum(codon_split(.x) != codon_split(.y)))
stopifnot(
  "An exported rung is identical to the original: nothing was recoded" =
    all(n_changed > 0),
  # as.integer on both sides: read_csv returns doubles, so identical() would
  # fail on storage type even when every count agrees.
  "Exported codons-changed counts disagree with the 08_ summary column" =
    identical(as.integer(unname(n_changed)),
              as.integer(rec_tbl$codons_changed[match(names(recoded),
                                                      rec_tbl$construct)]))
)
cat("Codons changed per rung:", paste(n_changed, collapse = ", "),
    "of", paste(map_int(recoded, ~ length(codon_split(.x))), collapse = ", "),
    "\n")

# The fixed parts must be byte-identical, not merely synonymous. If SmBiT, P2A
# or a linker had drifted, the construct would still translate correctly and
# every check above would pass.
fixed_ok <- map_lgl(names(recoded), function(nm) {
  rows <- layout_tbl %>% filter(construct == nm, state == "fixed")
  cv_n <- codon_split(recoded[[nm]]); cv_o <- codon_split(originals[[nm]])
  all(pmap_lgl(rows, function(start, end, ...)
    identical(cv_n[start:end], cv_o[start:end])))
})
stopifnot("A codon inside a fixed part was changed" = all(fixed_ok))
cat("Fixed parts (SmBiT, P2A, every linker) are byte-identical to the input.\n")
```

# 4. The Per-Codon Table

One row per codon per construct: where it is, what it was, what it became, and
why. This table is what both figures and the printout are drawn from, and it is
exported so the sequences can be read codon by codon outside R.

`status` has four levels, and the distinction between the last two matters when
reading the figures:

- **fixed** - inside SmBiT, P2A or a linker. Never offered to the recoder.
- **changed** - the recoder picked a different synonymous codon.
- **unchanged** - offered to the recoder, which picked the original codon back.
- **no synonym** - Met or Trp, the two amino acids with a single codon. These
  *cannot* change, so counting them as "unchanged" would overstate how often
  the recoder left a free choice alone.

```{r codon_table}
NOSYN_AA <- c("M", "W")   # the only amino acids with exactly one codon

codon_tbl <- map_dfr(names(recoded), function(nm) {
  cv_n <- codon_split(recoded[[nm]])
  cv_o <- codon_split(originals[[nm]])
  rows <- layout_tbl %>% filter(construct == nm)
  tibble(
    construct = nm,
    pos       = seq_along(cv_n),
    part      = rep(rows$part,  rows$ncod),
    state     = rep(rows$state, rows$ncod),
    codon_old = cv_o,
    codon_new = cv_n,
    aa        = GENETIC_CODE[cv_n],
    base3     = str_sub(cv_n, 3, 3)
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      state == "fixed"       ~ "fixed",
      aa %in% NOSYN_AA       ~ "no synonym",
      codon_new != codon_old ~ "changed",
      TRUE                   ~ "unchanged"
    ),
    status = factor(status,
                    levels = c("fixed", "no synonym", "unchanged", "changed")),
    base3  = factor(base3, levels = c("G", "C", "A", "T")),
    gc3    = base3 %in% c("G", "C")
  )

stopifnot(
  "Codon table lost rows relative to the sequences" =
    nrow(codon_tbl) == sum(map_int(recoded, ~ length(codon_split(.x)))),
  "A codon in the table does not translate as recorded" =
    all(codon_tbl$aa == GENETIC_CODE[codon_tbl$codon_new]),
  "Recoded and original codons disagree on the amino acid" =
    all(GENETIC_CODE[codon_tbl$codon_old] == codon_tbl$aa),
  "A status was not assigned" = !any(is.na(codon_tbl$status)),
  "Changed codons were found inside a fixed part" =
    !any(codon_tbl$state == "fixed" & codon_tbl$status == "changed")
)

cat("Codons by status and construct:\n")
print(codon_tbl %>% dplyr::count(construct, status) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
        as.data.frame())
```

The free codons the recoder left alone are worth separating out, because
"unchanged" is the only one of the four that is a *choice*:

```{r free_summary}
free_sum <- codon_tbl %>% filter(state == "free", !aa %in% NOSYN_AA) %>%
  group_by(construct) %>%
  summarise(free_choices = n(),
            changed      = sum(status == "changed"),
            pct_changed  = 100 * mean(status == "changed"),
            .groups = "drop")
print(free_sum %>% mutate(pct_changed = round(pct_changed, 1)) %>% as.data.frame())
```

# 5. Where Every Codon Is

Both panels share one geometry: `r params$codons_per_line` codons per row,
reading left to right and top to bottom, one facet per rung. Because the ladder
is nested, each facet begins with the whole of the facet above it, so a column
of tiles at the same grid position is the same codon in every construct that is
long enough to have it.

```{r grid_coords}
CPL <- params$codons_per_line
grid_tbl <- codon_tbl %>%
  mutate(row = (pos - 1L) %/% CPL + 1L,
         col = (pos - 1L) %%  CPL + 1L,
         construct = factor(construct, levels = names(recoded)))
```

## Third base, hue by class and shade within it

Blues are the GC-ending codons and purples the AT-ending ones, so GC3 is
readable as the blue fraction of the panel. Within each class the darker shade
is the purine (G, A).

```{r plot_tile_base3, fig.height=8}
base_cols <- c(G = "#03314D", C = "#0072B2",     # GC class: blues
               A = "#7D3C62", T = "#CC79A7")     # AT class: purples

p_base3 <- ggplot(grid_tbl, aes(col, -row, fill = base3)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.95, height = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ construct, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = base_cols, name = "Third base",
                    breaks = c("G", "C", "A", "T")) +
  labs(x = paste("Codon position within row (", CPL, "codons per row )"),
       y = NULL,
       title = "Third base of every codon in the recoded ladder",
       caption = paste("Blue = GC-ending, purple = AT-ending, so GC3 is the",
                       "blue fraction.\nRows read left to right, top to",
                       "bottom; the ladder is nested, so each panel starts",
                       "with the one above it.")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
        legend.position = "top")
print(p_base3)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_10_codon_map_base3_",
                            params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_base3, width = 10, height = 8)
```

## What the recoder touched

Same grid, colored by status. The fixed backbone is grey, so the free regions
stand out as the colored blocks, and within them the dark tiles are the codons
that actually changed.

```{r plot_tile_status, fig.height=8}
status_cols <- c("fixed"      = "grey85",
                 "no synonym" = "grey55",
                 "unchanged"  = "#A6CEE3",
                 "changed"    = "#0072B2")

p_status <- ggplot(grid_tbl, aes(col, -row, fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.95, height = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ construct, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_cols, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = paste("Codon position within row (", CPL, "codons per row )"),
       y = NULL,
       title = "Which codons the recoder changed",
       caption = paste("Grey = fixed part (SmBiT, P2A, linker), never offered.",
                       "Dark grey = Met or Trp,\nwhich have no synonym and so",
                       "cannot change. Pale blue = offered but the original",
                       "codon\nwas picked back. Dark blue = recoded.")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
        legend.position = "top")
print(p_status)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_10_codon_map_status_",
                            params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_status, width = 10, height = 8)
```

# 6. The Sequences, Printed Codon by Codon

The lab reference: every construct written out in codons, `r params$codons_per_line`
per line, with the same four states as the figure above. Colored text is
HTML-only and will not appear in a PDF render of this notebook.

```{r print_setup}
# Inline CSS per codon rather than classes, so a single copied block of HTML
# keeps its coloring when pasted elsewhere.
span_of <- function(codon, status, b3) {
  style <- switch(as.character(status),
    "fixed"      = "color:#9a9a9a;",
    "no synonym" = "color:#555555;text-decoration:underline;",
    "unchanged"  = "color:#222222;",
    "changed"    = paste0("color:", base_cols[[as.character(b3)]],
                          ";font-weight:700;")
  )
  paste0('<span style="', style, '">', codon, '</span>')
}

render_construct <- function(nm) {
  d <- codon_tbl %>% filter(construct == nm)
  spans <- pmap_chr(d %>% dplyr::select(codon_new, status, base3),
                    function(codon_new, status, base3)
                      span_of(codon_new, status, base3))
  lines <- split(seq_len(nrow(d)), (seq_len(nrow(d)) - 1L) %/% CPL)
  body <- map_chr(lines, function(ix) {
    paste0('<span style="color:#bbbbbb;">',
           formatC(d$pos[ix[1]], width = 5), '</span>  ',
           paste(spans[ix], collapse = " "))
  })
  paste0("<h3>", nm, "</h3>",
         '<pre style="font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,Consolas,monospace;',
         'font-size:11px;line-height:1.55;white-space:pre-wrap;',
         'word-break:break-all;background:#fcfcfc;border:1px solid #eee;',
         'padding:10px 12px;">',
         paste(body, collapse = "\n"), "</pre>")
}

legend_html <- paste0(
  '<p style="font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-size:12px;">',
  '<span style="color:#9a9a9a;">GCT</span> fixed part &nbsp;|&nbsp; ',
  '<span style="color:#555;text-decoration:underline;">ATG</span> no synonym ',
  '(Met, Trp) &nbsp;|&nbsp; ',
  '<span style="color:#222;">GCT</span> offered, original kept &nbsp;|&nbsp; ',
  '<span style="color:#03314D;font-weight:700;">GGG</span>/',
  '<span style="color:#0072B2;font-weight:700;">GCC</span>/',
  '<span style="color:#7D3C62;font-weight:700;">GAA</span>/',
  '<span style="color:#CC79A7;font-weight:700;">GAT</span> recoded, ',
  'colored by third base (G/C/A/T)</p>')
```

```{r print_sequences, results='asis'}
cat(legend_html)
cat(paste(map_chr(names(recoded), render_construct), collapse = "\n"))
```

# 7. Do the Chosen Codons Track MDA-MB-231 Usage?

The recoder picks a codon in two steps. The third base is decided first, by the
composition target: how many codons must end in each of A, C, G and T. Only
then is a codon drawn from the amino acid's options *with that third base*, in
proportion to the pooled synonymous usage of the expressed transcriptome.

Those two steps pull in different directions, so comparing the chosen codons
against raw usage conflates them. Both views are shown.

```{r read_usage}
usage <- read_csv(use_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  "Codon usage table is missing expected columns" =
    all(c("codon", "aa", "count", "prop") %in% names(usage)),
  "Synonymous proportions do not sum to 1 within every amino acid" =
    all(abs((usage %>% group_by(aa) %>%
               summarise(s = sum(prop), .groups = "drop"))$s - 1) < 1e-9)
)
# Biological spot-check, same one 08_ makes, so a wrong file cannot slip in.
stopifnot("CTG is not the most-used Leu codon: wrong or corrupt usage table" =
            (usage %>% filter(aa == "L") %>% slice_max(prop, n = 1))$codon == "CTG")
cat("Usage table: ", nrow(usage), " sense codons. CTG share of Leu: ",
    round(100 * usage$prop[usage$codon == "CTG"], 1), "%\n", sep = "")
```

The chosen codons are the **free** positions only, and the longest rung only.
Pooling the nested rungs would count eGFP copy 1 three times and copy 3 once,
weighting the sample by how often a copy happens to recur rather than by the
design.

```{r chosen_codons}
longest <- names(recoded)[length(recoded)]
chosen <- codon_tbl %>%
  filter(construct == longest, state == "free", !aa %in% NOSYN_AA)
cat("Scoring", nrow(chosen), "freely chosen codons from", longest, "\n")
```

## How much choice is left once the third base is fixed

Before comparing anything, this has to be established, because it bounds what
the comparison can possibly show. The menu is rebuilt here exactly as `08_`
builds it: codons below the `min_codon_prop` usage floor are dropped, unless
dropping them would leave a third base with no codon at all, in which case that
base keeps its most-used one.

```{r rebuild_menu}
menu_tbl <- usage %>%
  mutate(base3 = str_sub(codon, 3, 3)) %>%
  group_by(aa, base3) %>%
  mutate(keep = prop >= params$min_codon_prop,
         keep = if (any(keep)) keep else prop == max(prop)) %>%
  filter(keep) %>%
  mutate(exp_within = prop / sum(prop), n_opts = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

dropped <- usage %>% anti_join(menu_tbl, by = "codon")
cat("Codons below the", params$min_codon_prop, "floor and dropped from the menu:",
    if (nrow(dropped)) paste(dropped$codon, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n")

cells <- menu_tbl %>% dplyr::count(aa, base3, name = "n_opts")
cat("(amino acid, third base) cells:", nrow(cells),
    "| determined, one option only:", sum(cells$n_opts == 1),
    "| with a real choice:", sum(cells$n_opts > 1), "\n\n")
print(menu_tbl %>% filter(n_opts > 1) %>%
        group_by(aa, base3) %>%
        summarise(options = paste(codon, collapse = " / "),
                  usage_split = paste(round(100 * exp_within), collapse = " / "),
                  .groups = "drop") %>% as.data.frame())
```

**Fixing the third base determines the codon outright in `r sum(cells$n_opts == 1)`
of `r nrow(cells)` cells.** A choice survives in only `r sum(cells$n_opts > 1)`,
and all of them sit in the three six-codon families - Leu, Arg and Ser - which
are exactly the amino acids whose *first* base is also free. Everywhere else,
naming the third base names the codon.

So the usage-weighted sampler has very little to do, and the honest version of
"do the chosen codons track 231 usage?" splits in two: the raw comparison below
is dominated by the composition target, and the sampler itself can only be
judged on those `r sum(cells$n_opts > 1)` cells.

```{r floor_check}
# Nothing outside the rebuilt menu should appear in the construct. This is the
# check that would fire if the floor applied here drifted from the one 08_ used.
stopifnot("A chosen codon is not on the reconstructed menu: floor mismatch with 08_" =
            all(chosen$codon_new %in% menu_tbl$codon))
cat("Every chosen codon is on the menu 08_ drew from.\n")
```

## Raw: chosen proportion against transcriptome usage

Deviation here is **expected and by design**. The GC3 target is below eGFP's
native GC3, so AT-ending codons are deliberately over-represented relative to
their transcriptome share.

```{r plot_usage_raw}
obs_raw <- chosen %>% dplyr::count(aa, codon = codon_new, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(aa) %>% mutate(obs = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  inner_join(usage %>% dplyr::select(codon, exp = prop), by = "codon") %>%
  mutate(base3 = factor(str_sub(codon, 3, 3), levels = c("G", "C", "A", "T")))

rho_raw <- cor(obs_raw$exp, obs_raw$obs, method = "spearman")

p_raw <- ggplot(obs_raw, aes(exp, obs, color = base3)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = base_cols, name = "Third base",
                     breaks = c("G", "C", "A", "T")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Share of its amino acid in the MDA-MB-231 transcriptome",
       y = "Share among the chosen codons",
       title = "Chosen codons vs transcriptome usage, raw",
       subtitle = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.3f, n = %d codons",
                          rho_raw, nrow(obs_raw)),
       caption = paste("Points above the diagonal are over-used relative to",
                       "the transcriptome. The purple\nshift is the GC3 target",
                       "at work, not a sampler artifact: see the next panel.")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top")
print(p_raw)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_10_chosen_vs_usage_raw_",
                            params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_raw, width = 8, height = 6.5)
```

## Within each (amino acid, third base) cell: the sampler alone

Once the third base is fixed, the remaining choice is free, and *this* is where
usage should be reproduced. Expected proportions are renormalized within each
cell of the **rebuilt menu**, which is exactly the distribution the recoder
samples from. Using the unfiltered usage table here would be wrong: Leu's CTA
is below the floor and never offered, so A-ending Leu is forced to TTA, and
scoring it against CTA's transcriptome share would report a 45-point
"deviation" for a position that had no alternative.

Cells with a single option are dropped: they carry no choice and would sit
trivially at (1, 1).

```{r plot_usage_within}
obs_within <- chosen %>%
  dplyr::count(aa, base3, codon = codon_new, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(aa, base3) %>% mutate(obs_within = n / sum(n), n_cell = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  inner_join(menu_tbl %>% dplyr::select(codon, exp_within, n_opts),
             by = "codon") %>%
  filter(n_opts > 1)

stopifnot("No multi-option cells to score: the comparison is vacuous" =
            nrow(obs_within) > 0)

rho_w <- cor(obs_within$exp_within, obs_within$obs_within, method = "spearman")
mad_w <- mean(abs(obs_within$obs_within - obs_within$exp_within))

# The cells are small - a few codons each - so the question is not whether the
# observed split sits ON the diagonal but whether it sits as close as a correct
# usage-weighted draw of that size would. There is no closed form worth
# deriving here, so the null is simulated: redraw each cell from its own
# expectation, the same multinomial the recoder samples, and read off how far a
# correct sampler scatters. A fixed tolerance would be a guess; this is not.
set.seed(9)
sim_mad <- replicate(2000, {
  s <- obs_within %>% group_by(aa, base3) %>%
    group_modify(function(d, ...) {
      dr <- stats::rmultinom(1, d$n_cell[1], d$exp_within)[, 1]
      d$sim <- dr / sum(dr); d
    }) %>% ungroup()
  mean(abs(s$sim - s$exp_within))
})
p_mad <- (sum(sim_mad >= mad_w) + 1) / (length(sim_mad) + 1)
cat("Mean absolute within-cell deviation:", round(100 * mad_w, 1), "pp\n")
cat("Simulated under a correct sampler - median",
    round(100 * median(sim_mad), 1), "pp, 95th pct",
    round(100 * quantile(sim_mad, 0.95), 1), "pp\n")
cat("Empirical p that a correct sampler deviates at least this much:",
    round(p_mad, 3), "\n")

p_within <- ggplot(obs_within, aes(exp_within, obs_within, color = base3)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_cell), alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(values = base_cols, name = "Third base",
                     breaks = c("G", "C", "A", "T")) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, name = "Codons in cell") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Expected share within its (amino acid, third base) cell",
       y = "Observed share among the chosen codons",
       title = "Chosen codons vs usage, with the third base held fixed",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste("%d codons in %d cells. Mean deviation %.1f pp",
                                "vs %.1f pp expected of a correct sampler",
                                "(p = %.2f)"),
                          nrow(obs_within),
                          n_distinct(paste(obs_within$aa, obs_within$base3)),
                          100 * mad_w, 100 * median(sim_mad), p_mad),
       caption = paste("This is the only step the recoder actually samples;",
                       "everywhere else the third base\ndetermines the codon.",
                       "Point size is how many codons the cell held. Cells are",
                       "small,\nso the reference is the simulated spread of a",
                       "correct draw, not the diagonal itself.")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top")
print(p_within)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_10_chosen_vs_usage_within_",
                            params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_within, width = 8, height = 6.5)
```

```{r usage_checks}
# The observed deviation must be consistent with a correct usage-weighted draw.
# Two-sided in spirit but only the upper tail matters: a sampler that ignored
# `prob` would scatter further than the null, not closer.
stopifnot(
  "Within-cell deviation exceeds what a correct usage-weighted sampler produces" =
    p_mad > 0.01
)

# How much could this test actually detect? A sampler that drew uniformly
# instead of by usage is the realistic alternative, so its deviation is
# simulated too and asked against the same null. This is a POWER calculation,
# not a check that passes: it reports what the comparison can and cannot see.
set.seed(9)
sim_unif <- replicate(2000, {
  s <- obs_within %>% group_by(aa, base3) %>%
    group_modify(function(d, ...) {
      dr <- stats::rmultinom(1, d$n_cell[1], rep(1 / nrow(d), nrow(d)))[, 1]
      d$sim <- dr / sum(dr); d
    }) %>% ungroup()
  mean(abs(s$sim - s$exp_within))
})
p_unif <- (sum(sim_mad >= median(sim_unif)) + 1) / (length(sim_mad) + 1)
cat("A uniform sampler would deviate", round(100 * median(sim_unif), 1),
    "pp (median) vs", round(100 * median(sim_mad), 1),
    "pp for a usage-weighted one.\n")
cat("The null assigns that uniform median p =", round(p_unif, 3),
    "- so this test CANNOT reject uniform sampling at these cell sizes.\n")

# The direction must at least be right: uniform has to scatter further from the
# usage expectation than a usage-weighted draw does, or the two alternatives are
# not even ordered and the panel is measuring nothing.
stopifnot(
  "A uniform sampler is not distinguishable from a usage-weighted one here" =
    median(sim_unif) > median(sim_mad)
)
if (p_unif > 0.05)
  cat("NOTE: underpowered by design, not a defect.", sum(cells$n_opts > 1),
      "cells hold", sum(obs_within$n_cell) / 2,
      "codons between them;\n  a usage-weighted and a uniform draw of that size",
      "overlap heavily. The sampler's correctness\n  rests on reading",
      "`recode_codons` in 08_, which passes USE[opts] to sample(), not on this",
      "panel.\n")

cat("\nLargest within-cell deviations:\n")
print(obs_within %>%
        mutate(dev_pp = 100 * (obs_within - exp_within)) %>%
        arrange(desc(abs(dev_pp))) %>%
        dplyr::select(aa, codon, base3, n_cell, exp_within, obs_within, dev_pp) %>%
        mutate(across(c(exp_within, obs_within), ~ round(100 * .x, 1)),
               dev_pp = round(dev_pp, 1)) %>%
        head(10) %>% as.data.frame())
```
